RagShortTexts: Anchored in the Southern Uplands, the Black Douglas perfected savage border guerrilla.

Variants.Content: Emerging from the Southern Uplands, the Black Douglas under William the Hardy mastered ruthless night raids along the Tweed. Their rough border country bred hardy riders who knew every ford and sheepwalk up to the English frontier. Their light cavalry and schiltron spearmen struck terror into the northern English border marches, and English garrisons learned to fear a Douglas raid more than an open battle. The family fought for the Scottish crown and held wide estates in the Borders, so their campaigns tied local feuds to the wider war. That raiding style shaped Scottish border warfare long after William's time.

The Douglas lords preferred the forest and the ford to the tournament field. Their men were chosen for speed and quiet rather than heraldry, and a Douglas retinue could strike a border town and be back across the hills before the English garrison mustered.
